xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for OKF-11: Publish a bundle as a public static site with visibility and redaction

plan.title: Publish a bundle as a public static site with visibility and redaction
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: A bundle can only be viewed locally. Some projects want a public read-only site (for example a live-stream project whose viewers propose AI rules), but raw bundles hold operator-only notes, machine paths, incident detail and private names, so publishing them unchanged is unsafe.
narratives.Proposal: Add scripts/publish.py (stdlib + PyYAML) that builds a multi-page static site from public concepts only: per-concept pages with sources, trust tier and backlinks, filtered index pages, and client-side search from a prebuilt JSON index. Visibility comes from x_visibility with a fail-closed bundle default x_visibility_default in schema.md. A redaction profile (okf-publish.yaml plus built-in rules) rewrites all published text, and --check is a deterministic gate that exits 2 when a rule would fire in public text. Full design and exact interfaces are in .pan/drafts/OKF-11.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Deploying the site or adding host config files beyond the README sample workflow.
- Publishing log.md, non-Markdown assets (images, PDFs), embeddings or the .okf-index/ cache.
- Rendering generated/verified actor identities; only the derived trust tier is shown.
- A per-match allow list for redaction rules; bundles disable a whole built-in rule by id instead.
- Redacting or rewriting concept IDs or directory names; a rule match on one is a hard P_ID_REDACTION error.
- Excluding drafts or deprecated concepts automatically; visibility alone decides inclusion.
- Full CommonMark (HTML blocks, setext headings, reference-style links, indented code, hard breaks).
- Editing okf_common.py, validate.py, reindex.py, diff_lint.py, embed.py, build_index.py, search.py or templates/repo/.okf/scripts/*.
- Adding an okf.py CLI or vendoring the publish scripts into templates/repo/.okf/scripts/ (OKF-1/OKF-4 own these).
- Adding x_visibility checks to validate.py.
- Third-party scripts, CDN assets, inline scripts or innerHTML on the published site.
- Search stemming, fuzzy matching or ranking beyond term matching.
- Site theming or configuration options.
- Any treatment that makes a concept public without an explicit public value (no fail-open default).

autoDecisions.summary: Build now on the v0.1 scripts as new scripts/publish*.py files instead of waiting for OKF-1/OKF-4/OKF-6.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's 'fits after #6' is sequencing advice, not a requirement; isolated new files touch no existing script, so OKF-1's restructure can move them cheaply. v0.2 keys (verified, status, sources) are read tolerantly from frontmatter.

autoDecisions.summary: Bundle default key is x_visibility_default in root schema.md frontmatter.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names schema.md but no key; schema.md is itself a concept, so reusing x_visibility would be ambiguous. The x_ prefix matches x_embed.

autoDecisions.summary: Visibility fails closed: missing schema.md or key means private; invalid values are errors.
autoDecisions.rationale: Publishing must be opt-in on a public site; the CLI prints why zero concepts were published.

autoDecisions.summary: Markdown is rendered by a stdlib, fully escaping renderer; no CDN library.
autoDecisions.rationale: Stdlib + PyYAML constraint, deterministic output, and a testable XSS boundary for viewer-proposed text.

autoDecisions.summary: Built-in redaction rules apply with no profile; a bundle disables one by id.
autoDecisions.rationale: Fail toward redaction; per-rule disable handles ipv4 false positives without an allow list.

autoDecisions.summary: --check scans source text; 'passes after redaction' means after the author removes the matching text.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the issue's acceptance wording and keeps the gate deterministic; plain publish redacts and succeeds.

autoDecisions.summary: Add pytest under tests/ and run it in CI alongside selftest.sh.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires pytest and the v0.2 plan moves the repo to pytest; selftest.sh stays.
The issue asks for a prebuilt JSON index; file:// previews are documented as unsupported and UAT serves over http.server.

autoDecisions.summary: --out is rebuilt from scratch only when it carries the .okf-publish marker; otherwise a non-empty dir is refused.
autoDecisions.rationale: Stale pages from concepts turned private would leak; refusing unmarked directories prevents deleting user data.

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/OKF-11.md section 4.6 (render_markdown signature and the supported-construct table) and WI-2. Stdlib only. Every text run and attribute is html.escape'd; raw HTML renders as escaped text; images render alt text only; the renderer re-checks every href and renders any scheme other than http/https/mailto as plain text; resolver None renders link text only. Implement footnotes as specified. Write the six named tests in tests/test_publish_markdown.py.

verify_commands: uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pyyaml --with pytest python -m pytest -q tests/test_publish_cli.py

narrative.Action: Follow .pan/drafts/OKF-11.md section 4.8 steps 6-8 and WI-8. --check scans each public concept's title, description, type, status, tags, source title/resource/author and body, plus each filtered published index text, with publish_redact.scan. Body locations use file line numbers (body_start_line + line - 1); index locations use the index file's line numbers. Messages name the rule id and field and never the matched text. Exit 2 on any finding, else print `ok - publish check passed: <N> public concept(s), no redaction rule matches` and exit 0. Write nothing. Write the six named tests in tests/test_publish_cli.py.

metadata.sizeJustification: One feature in a small flat repo. The subsystem count is inflated because the lint counts the first two path segments, so each new scripts/publish_*.py and tests/test_publish_*.py file counts as its own subsystem; the real surface is scripts/, tests/, templates/, .github/ and four doc files. The items are not independently user-shippable: the model, renderer, redaction and search modules have no entry point until publish.py lands, and the issue's acceptance needs all of them together. Items are already split per module with their own tests.
